newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Air force says more flooding expected in Mozambique.
newsitem.headline: Air force says more flooding expected in Mozambique.

text.p: The South African Air Force, helping to evacuate flood victims in Mozambique, said it was ready to airlift more people after the sluice gates of the country's largest dam, the Cahora Bassa, were opened on Tuesday.
A dam official told Reuters the sluice gates were opened at 7 a.m. (0500 GMT) releasing 2,200 cubic metres of water per minute, which will worsen the flooding.
At the start of the rescue operation on Saturday dam officials cut the outflow to 1,600 cubic metres per minute.
"Air Force helicopters are presently warning the locals to evacuate the area and where necessary airlifting the people to safety," Air Force spokeswoman Laverne Machine said.
She said 650 people had been airlifted by the Air Force since Saturday, mainly in the Zambezi river valley which flows east towards the Indian Ocean. Dozens of the rescued had been hospitalised.
Machine said 17 crates of medical supplies had been distributed in the Caia area and more airdrops of medicine were planned.
Zimbabwe has also provided three military helicopters and a light aircraft to help with rescue operations in central Manica and Tete provinces.

Officials said in Sofala around the Caia area there are about 120,000 people affected by the floods in need of aid. Two people in the region had also been attacked by crocodiles and were taken to a hospital at Nyamawabue.
In the districts of Zumbo, Magoe and Moatize, 21 villages are reported to have been flooded and 600 hectares of crops destroyed.
The Mozambican cabinet was meeting on Tuesday to decide whether to declare a state of emergency.
